messages:
ryan: heads up — noticed a 5-10x tail latency jump on the long-context synth run around 18:42 UTC. memory for active shards climbs, eviction throughput drops, and overall token latency spikes. logs: https://internal/logs/kv/pager/1714567890
anika: can you paste a profiler sample or pprof? curious if this is eviction CPU, lock contention, or paging IO
ryan: pasted quick pprof summary below (truncated)
```
40.2%  evicter::evict_loop
28.5%  kv_cache::access
16.7%  parking_lot::Mutex::lock
8.1%   scheduler::poll
6.5%   other
--- mutex_wait_ns (count): global_lru_lock ~ 12000 waits, avg 4.3ms
```
cheng: that looks like global lock hold times growing under churn. in prior FIFO experiments we saw reinsert storms magnify lock hold time because reinserts push entries back on head and trigger more evictions
mike: can repro locally with a small harness: 32 concurrent requests, 128-token contexts, sliding-prefix reuse pattern. memory climbs and evicter thread becomes the hotspot. i'll run a debug build with lock profiling enabled
ryan: immediate mitigation ideas:
- lower evict_batch_size to reduce per-lock work
- try a try_lock fastpath for reads: if try_lock fails, treat as cache-miss and return; schedule background reinsert
- add a background reinsert queue so eviction doesn't do heavy reshuffle on hot path
example quick sketch:
```
if let Ok(_guard) = global_lru.try_lock() {
  // perform eviction work
} else {
  // hint: avoid blocking critical request path; enqueue a lightweight marker
  enqueue_reinsert_marker(key);
}
```
anika: also think about batching backpressure — if evicter stalls, many concurrent batch fillers race to populate KV and block. we can reduce max_batch_size or add a per-host queue depth limit until eviction_99p clears
cheng: i've opened a perf PR to add eviction_latency histogram (ms buckets) + eviction_lock_hold_time. also added a synthetic stress test that reproduces the 'sliding window' reuse pattern. running CI now: https://ci/internal/kv-evict-stress/1234
evicter-bot: CI job kv-evict-stress #1234 started by cheng — status: running
mike: i'll pick up the try_lock change and a canary that reduces max_batch_size when eviction_99p > 50ms. assigning to @mike. any objections? :thinking_face:
ryan: no objections. let's also capture flamegraphs for the nightly run and compare before/after. quick sync tomorrow 10am PT to review findings? :+1:
